title: Retention policy simulator and preview UI for prompts, responses, request logs, and metrics
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
Build a retention policy simulator and preview experience that lets customers author granular retention rules (by tenant, route, data type, region, and label) and immediately see what data would be retained, redacted, archived, or deleted. This solves customer needs for compliance reviews and evidence exports without guessing deletion impact and provides a safe dry-run mode before policies are enforced.

Scope:
- Console: new Retention Policies > Simulator tab with a rules editor, sample dataset selector, preview pane, and evidence export preview.
- API: retention policy dry-run endpoint that accepts a policy and returns a deterministic action set for a sample request ID list.
- Backend: deterministic retention evaluator (policy DSL interpreter) running against pinned snapshots for preview, and a production enforcement pipeline that reuses the same evaluator.
- Exports: retention preview report (CSV/JSON) and a sample evidence bundle manifest showing what would be exported or deleted.
- Residency-aware behavior: simulator respects per-tenant residency and regional retention overrides.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not implement archival lifecycle (S3 lifecycle rules) or actual data deletion jobs; those integrate after simulator validation.
acceptance_criteria:
- Customers can author a retention rule in Console and run a preview that lists affected object keys and summary counts for prompts, responses, request logs, and metrics.
- The dry-run API returns identical results to the Console preview for the same policy and sample dataset.
- Simulator honors tenant residency and per-tenant overrides; preview flags cross-region conflicts.
- Preview exports include a manifest and a sample evidence package manifest without transmitting customer PII outside residency constraints.
- Simulator has a dedicated audit trail entry showing who ran the preview, the policy version, and the sample dataset used.
- Feature toggles exist to enable dry-run for Dedicated and Private deployments before full enforcement.
notes:
Design decisions and trade-offs:
- Use a policy DSL close to what runtime will enforce (TTL + filters + transform actions) to avoid divergence between preview and enforcement.
- For privacy, previews operate on anonymized sample snapshots by default; customers can opt into live-sample previews with higher privileges.
- Deterministic evaluation is required so previews can be used as evidence during compliance reviews; this argues for reusing the production evaluator library in the preview service.
- We will not store large snapshot copies per customer long-term; use ephemeral snapshots generated from compact indices for preview runs.

Open questions:
- Should previews include token-level redaction simulation for prompt/response partial-retention policies? (Engineering input required on performance.)
- For metrics retention, do customers expect histogram-level previews or only series-level counts?

Implementation notes:
- Backend: implement an evaluator service in the compliance namespace that exposes /dry-run and /preview endpoints.
- Console: add a Simulator tab with a code editor (policy DSL) and an interactive table of results; include export and request-level drilldown.
- Security: require a policy preview permission and log runs to the audit store.
